# Check Report (`ferx check --json`)

`ferx check <model.ferx> [--data <data.csv>] --json` emits a structured JSON
report describing every validation finding, instead of the human-readable
summary. The report is designed to be consumed programmatically — by editor
tooling, CI, or a coding agent authoring model files — so findings carry a
stable machine-readable `code` rather than only prose.

This is the same data the Rust API returns from
[`validate_model_file`](../api/parsing.qmd); see also the
[CLI reference](../cli.qmd) for the human-readable form and exit codes.

## Top-level shape

```json
{
  "valid": false,
  "model": "mymodel",
  "data": "data/mydata.csv",
  "diagnostics": [
    {
      "severity": "error",
      "code": "E_MISSING_COVARIATE",
      "message": "Model references covariate(s) not found in data (case-sensitive): WGT. Available covariate columns: (none).",
      "suggestion": "available covariate columns: (none)"
    }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| `valid` | bool | `true` when there are **no** `error`-severity diagnostics (warnings and info rows alone keep it `true`). |
| `model` | string | Model file stem. |
| `data` | string | Present only when `--data` was supplied. |
| `diagnostics` | array | Every finding; see below. May be empty. |

## Diagnostic object

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| `severity` | `"error"` \| `"warning"` \| `"info"` | Only `error` affects `valid` and the exit code. `info` is a fact about the model or data, not a finding — count it apart from the warnings ([#2387](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/2387)). An `info` row keeps the `W_` prefix of its code. |
| `code` | string | Stable identifier (see table below). |
| `message` | string | Human-readable description. |
| `block` | string | *Optional.* Owning model block, e.g. `"error_model"`. Omitted when not attributable to one block. |
| `line` | integer | *Optional.* 1-based source line — see the caveat below. |
| `suggestion` | string | *Optional.* Actionable hint. |

Optional fields are omitted entirely when absent (not emitted as `null`).

## Error / warning codes

Grouped by what the finding is about. Codes are stable; new ones may be added over time.
Treat an unrecognised code as a generic finding of its given `severity`.

The tables below list every code the engine emits — the ones `ferx check` reports, the
ones an entry point returns as `EngineError::code()`, and the ones that open a message in
a run's `warnings` — and the in-code registry in `src/diagnostics.rs` lists the same set.
A unit test fails when either drifts from the codes in `src/`
([#1051](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1051)).

- [Model-file structure](#codes-model-file-structure)
- [Parameters and random effects](#codes-parameters-and-random-effects)
- [Method and optimizer compatibility](#codes-method-and-optimizer-compatibility)
- [Data and dosing](#codes-data-and-dosing)
- [Scaling, output and derived columns](#codes-scaling-output-and-derived)
- [Experimental and degraded paths](#codes-experimental-and-degraded)
- [Warnings a run records](#codes-run-warnings)
- [Codes only an entry point raises](#codes-entry-point)

### Model-file structure {#codes-model-file-structure}

The file could not be read as a ferx model at all, or names a block ferx does not have.

`[fit_options]` and `[error_model]` lines are consumed end to end or reported as `E_PARSE` with the offending line quoted. A `[fit_options]` line that is not a `key = value` pair names the repair (`` `method saem` is not a `key = value` pair — did you mean `method = saem`? ``); an `[error_model]` line matching no statement form lists the accepted forms. Before 0.4.0 both were dropped without a diagnostic, and the `method` case is the sharp one — the fit then ran the **default estimator** while `ferx check` reported the file VALID, so a run the author read as SAEM was FOCEI and its objective was not comparable to the one they asked for. See [#1390](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1390), [Fit options](../model-file/fit-options.qmd#syntax) and [Error model](../model-file/error-model.qmd#syntax).

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_PARSE` | error | The model file failed to parse (catch-all for parser errors). |
| `E_MODEL_READ` | error | The model file could not be read: it does not exist, cannot be opened, or is not UTF-8. The message names the path and the operating system's reason, and no `block` is set. Before [#1752](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1752) this was reported as `E_PARSE`. The check reads the file once, and parses and binds that one read, so a file moved or edited while the check runs does not change its result. |
| `E_FIT_OPTION` | error | A call-time fit-option override handed to `validate_model_file_with()` could not be applied: the key is not a `[fit_options]` / `[data_selection]` key, or its value is one the key does not accept. One diagnostic per pair, no `block`; like a parse failure it is terminal, so the report carries only these ([#2165](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/2165)). A model file's own `[fit_options]` refuses the same values at parse time as `E_PARSE`. |
| `E_MISSING_BLOCK` | error | A required `[block]` is absent. `block` names which one. `run_model_simulate()` (`ferx --simulate`) returns it on block `simulation` for a model file with no `[simulation]` block ([#1788](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1788)). |
| `E_UNKNOWN_BLOCK` | error | A `[block]` header is not a recognised block name. The message lists every offending header with its line, the valid set **this build accepts**, and a did-you-mean when there is a near match; `suggestion` carries the near match on its own. See [#1040](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1040). |
| `E_DEPRECATED_BLOCK` | error | A `[block]` that *was* ferx syntax and is no longer read — currently `[initial_values]`, whose contents moved inline into `[parameters]`. Reported separately from `E_UNKNOWN_BLOCK` so the message can name the replacement instead of offering a did-you-mean that does not exist. |
| `E_BLOCK_INSTANCE_NAME` | error | A `[block NAME]` instance name is given for a block that takes none (e.g. `[fit_options DOSE]`), or omitted for one that requires it (`[covariate_nn NAME]`). |
| `E_BLOCK_FEATURE_DISABLED` | error | A recognised block needs a cargo feature this binary was not built with — `[event_model]` / `[binary_model]` need `--features survival`, `[markov_model]` needs `--features markov`. (`[covariate_nn]` has its own `E_NN_FEATURE_DISABLED`.) |
| `E_NN_FEATURE_DISABLED` | error | A `[covariate_nn]` block requires building with `--features nn`. |
| `W_PARSE` | warning | A warning the parser recorded while building the model that has no dedicated code. `ferx check` reports it under `W_PARSE` with the parser's own message, which names the block involved. `fit()` reports the same text in `FitResult.warnings`. |
| `W_DATA_PATH_OVERRIDE` | warning | A data path was passed explicitly (`--data`, or from R) and the model file's `[data]` block names a different file — compared as written, then as canonicalized paths. The explicit path is used. |

### Parameters and random effects {#codes-parameters-and-random-effects}

A theta, eta, kappa or sigma the model uses is not declared, is declared in the wrong order, or has no data to bind to.

A `[parameters]` line must also be consumed end to end by exactly one declaration form, at both ends: text before or after a complete declaration is reported as `E_PARSE` with the offending line quoted, and so is a line matching no form at all. The one shape with a code of its own is a scale tag on a `block_*` declaration, below. Before 0.4.0 all of it was dropped without a diagnostic — including leading text, which could silently turn `block_sigma PROP ~ 0.04` into a diagonal `sigma`.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_ETA_NOT_DECLARED` | error | An unresolved identifier reads as a random effect (`ETA…` / `KAPPA…`) but no `omega` / `kappa` declaration defines it, and the data carries no such column. Usually a deleted `omega` line whose `exp(ETA_…)` term was left behind. |
| `W_ETA_NOT_DECLARED` | warning | As `E_ETA_NOT_DECLARED`, but reported without `--data`, where ferx cannot yet know whether the dataset supplies the column. |
| `E_SIGMA_ORDER_MISMATCH` | error | A single-endpoint `[error_model]` names its sigmas in an order other than the `[parameters]` declaration order. These sigmas are consumed *positionally*, so the written names must match the declared order. Fix by reordering the `sigma` **declarations** (permuting a `block_sigma`'s lower triangle with them) — reordering the *arguments* also parses but swaps the proportional and additive roles, i.e. changes the model. See [#1001](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1001) and [Error model](../model-file/error-model.qmd#sigma-order). |
| `E_BLOCK_VARIANCE_ONLY` | error | A scale tag (`(sd)`, `(variance)` or `(var)`) on a `block_omega`, `block_sigma` or `block_kappa` declaration. The lower triangle mixes variances and covariances, so one tag cannot say which entry is on which scale. The repair depends on the tag, and the report's `suggestion` carries whichever applies: after `(sd)`, square each SD into a variance and write the off-diagonals as covariances; after `(variance)` or `(var)`, delete the tag - the lower triangle was already on that scale, so the tag said nothing and nothing else needs changing. The code is raised only when deleting the tag leaves a declaration that parses, so the repair is always sufficient; a tag alongside other stray text is `E_PARSE`. Until 0.4.0 the tag was dropped in silence and the file reported VALID, so an SD-coded block fitted from squared-wrong initial estimates. See [#1377](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1377) and [Parameters](../model-file/parameters.qmd). |
| `E_IOV_MISSING_OCC` | error | Model declares kappa (IOV) parameters but no occasion labels were found. Set `iov_column` to read them from a dataset column, or `iov_occasion = dose` / `time(...)` to derive them in the model, both in `[fit_options]`. On `--simulate` the `[simulation]` design has no dataset and gives each subject a single dose, so the message names only `iov_occasion = time(...)`, with a breakpoint inside the `times` grid. It says that `iov_occasion = dose` derives a single occasion there, and that an `iov_column` the model sets has no effect ([#2005](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/2005)). Not raised for a model with nested levels, whose groups come from its level columns. |
| `W_IOV_OCC_MISSING` | warning | Some rows in the IOV occasion column had missing or unparseable values; those rows were assigned occasion=0. |
| `E_THETA_LEVEL_BINDING` | error | A `theta NAME[COL, ...]` level block could not be bound to the data's levels: a level column missing or non-finite, no observation rows, or a contrast the data cannot carry. Block `parameters`. The binders return the same code from a running program, where it also covers binding to a fit's level layout (a level the fit estimated no θ for), which `ferx check` cannot reach. |
| `E_COVARIATE_STATS_BINDING` | error | A `[covariate_model]` statistic could not be bound to the data: a `levels = auto` relation whose data carry one level, or a covariate with no non-missing value. Block `covariate_model`. The binders return the same code, including for a fit's statistics that do not match the model. |

#### Priors, weights and unused parameters

A declared parameter that nothing reads, a prior that names no parameter, or a kappa weight or initial estimate the data make unusable.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_PRIOR_UNRESOLVED` | error | A declared prior cannot be applied: it names no `theta` / `omega` / `sigma` / `kappa` in `[parameters]`, names a `FIX`ed parameter, an element of a `block_omega` / `block_sigma` / `block_kappa`, or a name that resolves to several coordinates; it is declared twice; its central value is not finite (or not positive for a log-packed parameter); or a `[priors] from_fit` was not expanded. The message names the parameter. |
| `W_UNUSED_PARAM` | warning | A user-declared θ, ω or κ is not referenced by any `[individual_parameters]` or `[event_model]` expression, or a σ is not referenced in `[error_model]`. It does not affect predictions and is not meaningfully estimated. Generated θ (NN weights, diffusion) and the `iiv_on_ruv` η are not checked. |
| `E_KAPPA_WEIGHT_NONPOSITIVE` | error | A `kappa NAME ~ value weight = W` sample-size weight evaluates to zero, a negative number or a non-finite value at some observation or dose record, at the model's initial θ. κ is applied as `κ/√W`, so such a weight divides an individual parameter by zero. The usual cause is a missing or non-numeric cell in the covariate the weight reads. The first offending record is reported. |
| `W_KAPPA_WEIGHT_VARIES_WITHIN_OCCASION` | warning | A weighted kappa's weight expression evaluates to different values (relative difference above `1e-9`) at two observation records of the same occasion, or of the same group of the kappa's level when nested levels are declared. κ is drawn once per occasion or group, so its effective variance Ω_IOV/W is ambiguous; each record is scaled by its own weight. Reported once per kappa, naming the first subject. |
| `W_ADDITIVE_INIT_SCALE` | warning | A `combined` error model's additive SD initial estimate is below 1% of the data scale (the median `abs(DV)` of the observations that endpoint covers). From such a start a multimodal fit can settle where the additive term collapses and the proportional one inflates. The value is not changed; if the fit converges with the additive variance near zero, retry from about 10% of the median `abs(DV)`. |

#### Covariate statistics and level blocks

A `[covariate_model]` statistic or a `theta NAME[...]` level block that has to be bound to the data, and the data it is bound to.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_COVSTAT_UNRESOLVED` | error | A `[covariate_model]` relation still needs statistics derived from the data — `center = median`, `levels = auto`, or a form whose default bounds come from the data — and none were bound. Reported with `--data`, where the binding was attempted. |
| `W_COVSTAT_UNBOUND` | warning | As `E_COVSTAT_UNRESOLVED`, but reported without a `--data` file: the model is fine, it just cannot be built until a dataset supplies the statistics. |
| `E_COV_LEVEL_UNKNOWN` | error | The data carry a value of a categorical `[covariate_model]` covariate that is not one of the relation's levels, which the generated factor would silently model as the reference level ([#1111](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1111), [#1740](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1740)). Raised by `fit()`, `ferx check`, the `simulate*`, adaptive and `predict*` entry points, `compute_npde_npd`, `run_sir` and `run_covariance`. |
| `E_THETA_GATHER_INDEX_MISSING` | error | A `theta NAME[...]` block gathered by a bare data column, where some observation or dose record of a subject has no value in that column. Every record that reads the block needs one. Reported at most once per block and subject. |
| `E_THETA_GATHER_INDEX_RANGE` | error | A `theta NAME[...]` block's index column holds a value on some record that is not finite, not a whole number, or outside `1..=N` for the block's `N` levels. The index is 1-based — a 0-based column is the usual cause — or `theta NAME[N]` declares too few levels. Reported at most once per block and subject. |
| `E_THETA_LEVELS_DATA_UNBOUND` | error | A model whose `theta NAME[...]` level block is bound was handed a population never bound for it, so no record carries an index into the block's levels — the usual "fit, then predict or simulate new data" without binding the new data. The message names the binder to call (`bind_from_fit` after a fit, `bind_theta_levels` on a fresh parse), or "`k` of `n` subjects" and the first such ID when only some subjects carry the index ([#1647](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1647), [#1762](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1762)). Raised by `fit()` and the `predict*`, `simulate*`, adaptive, NPDE and post-hoc entry points. |
| `E_THETA_LEVELS_DATA_MISMATCH` | error | A population that carries a bound level block's index was bound for other levels than the model's ([#1762](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1762)): a record's index is not the position, in the model's level table, of the label its own level columns spell, or an index arrives without its level column. Unseen labels are listed, or the first misindexed record is named. Refused, never re-indexed. Raised by the same entry points as `E_THETA_LEVELS_DATA_UNBOUND`. |

#### Residual correlation

A residual `correlation` line, or a `block_sigma` correlated residual, against the rows it correlates.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_RANGE` | error | The θ behind a residual `correlation <kind>(RHO) by …` line can leave the residual covariance `R` indefinite: a `cs` ρ at or below `−1/(n−1)` for the largest block of `n` rows, a negative `car1` ρ, or a fixed / simulated value with `abs(ρ) ≥ 1`. A free ρ must also be bounded within `±0.995`, since `R` becomes numerically singular as `abs(ρ)` approaches 1; `FIX` it to hold a value closer to ±1. |
| `E_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_RESET` | error | Under a residual `correlation ar1(…)` or `car1(…)` line, one block holds rows on both sides of a TIME reset (an `EVID=3/4` record that restarts TIME), so their order and the lag between them are undefined. Add the occasion column to `by` so each occasion is its own block, or use `cs`. |
| `E_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_TIES` | error | Under a residual `correlation ar1(…)` or `car1(…)` line, two rows of one block share a TIME. `ar1` orders a block by TIME, so tied rows have no order; `car1` correlates them by `ρ^0 = 1`, which makes `R` singular. Give them distinct times or use `cs`. |
| `W_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_INERT` | warning | The model declares a serial residual `correlation` line, but in every subject each block formed by its `by` column(s) holds at most one observation. No two rows are correlated, so ρ does not enter the likelihood and cannot be estimated. Check that the `by` columns group the rows meant to be correlated. |
| `W_BLOCK_SIGMA_L2_ORDER` | warning | Some subjects with no `L2` grouping id have a (time, occasion) group in which one observation shares a `block_sigma` correlation with two or more others, so the cross covariances are paired one-to-one in CSV row order and reordering rows would change the fit. Add an explicit `L2` column giving each correlated unit its own id. |
| `W_L2_UNUSED` | warning | The data carry an `L2` column, which the reader always treats as the reserved level-2 grouping id for `block_sigma` pairing, but the model declares no correlated residual. The column therefore does nothing and is not readable as a covariate; rename it if a covariate was meant. |

#### Profiled level blocks

A level block declared `profile` ([#1065](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1065)) has its levels solved for at every outer step rather than searched by the optimizer. That needs a linear route to the prediction and a least-squares objective, so the check refuses anything else; nothing falls back to ordinary estimation.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_PROFILE_SCOPE` | error | A profiled block that cannot be fitted that way: `profile` on a single θ, or with `FIX`; a box that is a point, is empty or misses the init; a method other than `foce` / `focei`, or `n_agq > 1`; a non-Gaussian endpoint; a residual error that is not additive, or log-transformed; M3 censoring; a `[mixture]`, `[diffusion]` or FREM model; `optimizer = trust_region` or `mma`; `global_search`; a parameter prior. Block `parameters`. |
| `E_PROFILE_NOT_LINEAR` | error | A profiled block that a prediction does not read as `c × block` plus terms that do not read it, with `c` from the data alone. The message names the construct (a function, power or remainder, an inline `if` or `if` branch whose condition reads more than data, a product of two reads, a parameter coefficient, a divisor, the states, the residual error, a second profiled block) and where it is, or says that no prediction reads the block. Block `parameters`. |

#### Nested variability levels

A model that declares `level` lines ([nested levels](../model-file/iov.qmd#nested-levels), [#1082](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1082)) is checked for how its levels are declared and whether the data can identify them.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_LEVEL_MIXED_WITH_IOV_COLUMN` | error | A `level` declaration together with `iov_column` or `iov_occasion` in `[fit_options]`, an `iov_occasion` rule other than `column` in the fit options or `SimulateOptions` of a model with nested levels (block `fit_options`), or a `kappa` with no `at LEVEL` in a model that declares levels. A `level` replaces the occasion options, and once levels exist every kappa names its own. Block `parameters`. |
| `E_LEVEL_MISSING_LABEL` | error | A record (observation, dose, `EVID=2` / `MDV=1` row or reset) has no numeric value in a level column (a blank cell is missing, not carried forward from the row before; a text label such as `NCT01` has to be written as a numeric code). Its group at each level is identified by its labels from the outermost level down, so every record needs all of them. The message names the level, the column, the record and its time. Raised by the fit, `ferx check --data` and every `simulate*` entry point. Block `parameters`. |
| `E_LEVEL_SINGLE_MEMBER` | error | A level has at most one group inside every group of its parent, and one of its kappas enters the model through the same parameters as a random effect of the parent level (the subject's η for the first level). The two variances cannot be told apart. A level where some parents hold several groups is not refused. Block `parameters`. |
| `W_LEVEL_SUMMARY` | info | Informational, not a finding, so reported with severity `info` and not counted as a warning ([#2387](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/2387)): one row per level of a model with nested levels, outermost first, e.g. ``level `ARM`: 7 groups in 3 `STUDY` groups (per `STUDY` group: min 1, median 2, max 4); 1 of 3 `STUDY` groups holds a single `ARM` group; 1 kappa at `ARM` (K_ARM). Counted on the observation records.`` The parent of the first level is the subject. `E_LEVEL_SINGLE_MEMBER` refuses a level only when **every** parent holds a single group and a kappa has a twin; a level where some parents hold one group and others several is identified and fits, and this row is where its count shows. Counted on the observation records, as the refusal counts them; a parent with no observation record is left out. Not reported while a level label is missing (`E_LEVEL_MISSING_LABEL`). Raised by `ferx check --data` only, not recorded by `fit()` ([#2035](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/2035)). Block `parameters`. |
| `E_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_GROUPING_AMBIGUOUS` | error | A residual `correlation … by` line on a model with nested levels whose grouping a level and a data column would read two ways: a level name inside a list of columns (`by (STUDY, ARM)`), a level name that is also a different data column, or the `by` column of a level nested in another level written under another name. `by L` naming a level groups by that level's groups, nested by key; a column groups by its value within `ID`, which merges two groups that share a label in different parents. The message names the level and says what to write. Raised by the fit, `ferx check --data` and `simulate()`. Block `error_model`. |
| `E_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_CONFOUNDED_KAPPA` | error | A `correlation cs(…) by …` line whose blocks group the observation rows exactly as the groups of a level that carries a kappa (a nested level, or the occasions of a one-level model), compared as partitions in every subject, so `cs by ARMID` beside `kappa … at ARM` counts. A kappa gives each group's rows one shared random effect, which is the correlation `cs` estimates: `ρ` and the kappa variance are not identified together. `ar1` and `car1` are not refused, and neither is `cs` over a grouping no kappa is at. Block `error_model`. |
| `W_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_PARTLY_CONFOUNDED_KAPPA` | warning | The same comparison holds in some subjects but not all, e.g. `cs by STUDY` next to a kappa at `ARM` where some studies have one arm. The model is identified, from the other subjects, and fits; the message gives the count, since ρ and the kappa variance are separated by those subjects alone. A subject whose partitions agree only trivially (every row its own block, e.g. one observation) counts on neither side, here or for the refusal. Raised by the fit and `ferx check --data`. |

#### Initial estimates against the optimizer box

Every initial estimate is packed and compared against the box the optimizer will
search inside, before the first objective evaluation. All of the codes below are
data-independent, so `ferx check model.ferx` reports them without a `--data`
file. The two that are **not** skipped when `maxiter = 0` are called out where
they appear; for the rest the exemption is because an evaluation-only run clamps
the start like any other, it just does not hold the clamped value through a
search.

##### Against the box the optimizer searches

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_OMEGA_INIT_AT_RAIL` | error | A **free** `omega` / `kappa` / `[mixture] omega(k)` variance whose initial value packs onto the optimizer's `-6` lower rail — every variance ≤ 6.1e-6, and `~ 0.0` in particular (a declared zero is regularised to 1e-8, packing to `ln(L) = -9.21`). The start is clamped onto the rail and the coordinate cannot be estimated from there: it stays collapsed or runs away to the opposite rail, moving the θ estimates with it. Either `FIX` it (that is the supported way to declare no variability) or start it at ≥ 1e-5. NM-TRAN rejects the same stream with error 76, `INITIAL ESTIMATE OF VARIANCE CANNOT BE ZERO UNLESS FIXED`. Σ is **not** included — a free `sigma ~ 0.0 (sd)` is clamped onto its own `-8` rail and recovers the optimum. **Only reported when an optimizer will actually search**: `maxiter = 0` (NONMEM `MAXEVAL=0`, as used by `ferx gam --no-fit`) is not reported — it clamps the start like any other run, but produces one objective and stops, so nothing is trapped on the rail; note that it therefore *evaluates* a free `~ 0.0` at `exp(-12)` rather than at the declared value, which `FIX` avoids. `saem` / `imp` / `impmap` / `bayes` carry their own iteration counts and are still checked. A model used only with `predict()` / `simulate()` is *not* exempt on the check path: `ferx check` reports what `fit()` would refuse, so such a model is reported here while still simulating fine. Add `maxiter = 0` to `[fit_options]` if the file is genuinely simulation-only. The message is chosen **per eta**, not per matrix: an eta declared inside a `block_omega` / `block_kappa` is told its block is near-singular (in a block it is the *correlations* that drive `L_ii` to zero, so raising a declared variance is not the fix), while a diagonally declared one is told to write `~ 0.0 FIX`. Mixing a block and diagonal `omega` lines in the same model — the whole Ω then packs as one Cholesky — does not change what the diagonal eta is told. A **one-eta** `block_omega (NAME) = [...]` is correlated with nothing, so it gets the declared-zero explanation rather than the near-singular one, spelled in its own form (`` write `block_omega (NAME) = [0.0] FIX` ``) ([#1394](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1394)). See [#1229](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1229) and [Parameters](../model-file/parameters.qmd#diagonal-omega). |
| `E_THETA_INIT_OUTSIDE_BOUNDS` | error | A `theta` whose initial value is **strictly outside** its own declared range. The optimizer clamps the start into its box, so `theta TVCL(0.05, 0.1, 10.0)` fits from `0.1` — a factor of two — silently, on every run. NM-TRAN refuses the identical stream before any estimation (error 24). Judged against the **declared** numbers, not the packed ones: `theta TVCL(-5.0, 0.0, 10.0)` is reported even though `-5` and the declared lower `0` both pack onto the same `1e-10` floor, and the message names where the fit really begins (`1e-10`, which is neither the declared value nor the declared bound). A start **exactly on** a bound is *not* reported: there the clamp is a no-op, so nothing moves. Shares `E_OMEGA_INIT_AT_RAIL`'s `maxiter = 0` exemption. See [#1251](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1251). |
| `W_INIT_OUTSIDE_BOUNDS` | warning | An initial estimate strictly outside one of ferx's **internal** rails rather than a declared bound: the hidden `1e9` θ cap, the Ω `±6` (variance ≤ 1.6e5) / off-diagonal `±10` guards, or the Σ `[-8, 5]` guard. Clamped there before the first objective evaluation. The Σ rails are on the **SD** scale, which is how ferx stores σ — a plain `sigma X ~ v` declares the variance `v` and the message quotes `sqrt(v)`, so `sigma PROP_ERR ~ 1e6` reads `an SD of 1.000e3`. A warning and not an error because these recover: `omega ~ 1e8` on `examples/warfarin.ferx` reaches the base optimum under all eight optimizer × method arms. The Ω *lower* rail is `E_OMEGA_INIT_AT_RAIL` instead, where the fit is genuinely trapped. There is no `1e-10` θ counterpart here: a start below the floor packs *equal* to its floored bound, so it is `W_INIT_NOT_REPRESENTABLE` below instead, and a range lying entirely below it is `E_INIT_BOUNDS_INVERTED`. |

##### When the box is empty

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_INIT_BOUNDS_INVERTED` | error | A coordinate whose packed box is **empty**, so no start can be placed in it at all. Only a `theta` can reach this through the parser — every other segment's bounds are constants — but the code is not θ-specific, and a non-θ coordinate is reported the same way. Three causes: the declared bounds are swapped (`theta TVCL(1.0, 5.0, 2.0)`); the declared range lies entirely above ferx's `1e9` packing cap; or it lies entirely below the `1e-10` floor — `theta TVCL(1e-12, 1e-13, 1e-11)`, an ordinary small parameter, is the last. Reported **even at `maxiter = 0`**, unlike every other code in this table: an empty box is not clamped, it aborts the clamp, and an evaluation-only run clamps too. Only the affected coordinate is silenced — every other parameter in the file is still reported in the same pass. |

##### When the packed space cannot represent the declared value

A different question from the three above, and the one they are structurally
blind to: `pack_params` applies its own guards *before* any box exists, and the
box is then built from the already-moved value — so a coordinate reported here
is, by construction, perfectly in-box.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `W_INIT_NOT_REPRESENTABLE` | warning | A declared value the **packer itself** altered, before any box existed (#1307): the `1e-10` log floor on a θ / Ω-diagonal / Σ / `[mixture]` override, or the Fisher-z `±3` rail on a **free** `block_sigma` correlation. The message names the declared value and the value the optimizer actually sees. A separate code from `W_INIT_OUTSIDE_BOUNDS` because every coordinate it names is, by construction, *inside* its box — the box is built from the moved value — so a silent `W_INIT_OUTSIDE_BOUNDS` does not mean the declared values reached the optimizer. Not exempt at `maxiter = 0`: an evaluation-only run scores the substituted value too. A `FIX`ed correlation is never reported, since #1307 holds it exactly. |

### Method and optimizer compatibility {#codes-method-and-optimizer-compatibility}

The chosen estimation method or optimizer cannot serve this model.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_SAEM_NO_RANDOM_EFFECTS` | error | `method = saem` (anywhere in a method chain) on a model with no random effects (`n_eta = 0`). SAEM is an EM over the random effects; use `foce` / `focei` / `laplace`. |
| `E_METHOD_NO_RANDOM_EFFECTS` | error | `method = imp`, `impmap` or `bayes` (anywhere in a method chain) on a model with no random effects (`n_eta = 0`). Each integrates over the random effects, so with none declared the marginal collapses to the observation likelihood; use `foce` / `focei` / `laplace`. See [#1007](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1007). |
| `W_GN_NO_RANDOM_EFFECTS` | warning | `method = gn` as the last estimating stage on a model with no random effects (`n_eta = 0`). Pure Gauss-Newton is start-sensitive there — with no inner EBE loop the BHHH step can collapse far from the optimum. Prefer `gn_hybrid` or `focei`. Not reported when a later stage re-optimises the GN result (`gn_hybrid`, or a `methods = [gn, focei]` chain). See [#1006](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1006). |
| `W_AUTO_OPTIMIZER_FOLLOWS_GRADIENT` | warning | `gradient = fd` set while `optimizer` is left at `auto`, on a model whose analytic outer gradient *is* in scope. `auto` resolves off the gradient's availability, so the one line moved the optimizer (to `bobyqa`) as well as the gradient. The message names both the optimizer that ran and the one an unforced arm would use; pin `optimizer` in both arms of a comparison. See [#1381](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1381) and [`gradient = fd` moves the optimizer too](../estimation/optimizers.qmd#gradient-fd-moves-the-optimizer). |
| `E_IMP_CHAIN` | error | `imp` is mis-placed in a method chain — repeated, or (with `imp_eval_only = true`) not the terminal stage. The estimating `imp` may sit anywhere; an evaluation-only `imp` must be terminal. |
| `E_OPTIMIZER_IOV` | error | `optimizer = trust_region` used with an IOV model (`n_kappa > 0`). |
| `E_NESTED_LEVEL_METHOD_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A model with nested levels (more than one `level`) fitted with a method other than `foce` / `focei` at `n_agq = 1`: SAEM, IMP, IMPMAP, Bayes, VI, Laplace, FOCEI quadrature or GN anywhere in the chain, or with a `[mixture]` or FREM. The message names the first such stage. A single level is not affected. Block `fit_options`. |
| `E_OPTIMIZER_AGQ` | error | `optimizer = trust_region` used with a quadrature stage (`method = laplace`, or `method = focei` with `n_agq > 1`). The trust region scores the quadrature objective but its gradient is the FOCE/Laplace closed form, so it would converge to the FOCE optimum while reporting quadrature OFVs. |
| `E_SDE_INCOMPATIBLE` | error | An SDE (`[diffusion]`) model used with an incompatible method (`saem`, `gn`, `gn_hybrid`) or gradient setting. |
| `E_AD_RETIRED` | error | `gradient_method = ad` was requested. The Enzyme automatic-differentiation path was retired; use `auto` (the analytic sensitivities, with finite differences outside their scope) or `fd`. The token still parses so an old model file gets this message rather than a parse error. |

#### Quadrature

A quadrature stage — `method = laplace`, or `method = focei` with `n_agq > 1` — or an `n_agq` setting the chain cannot use.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_AGQ_NODES_ZERO` | error | `n_agq = 0`, under any method. Zero nodes must not silently disable FOCEI quadrature or be coerced to one-node Laplace, and a method that ignores `n_agq` still records it in the fit, where a `.fitrx` holding 0 does not load ([#1770](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1770)); use `n_agq = 1`. |
| `E_AGQ_NODES_TOO_LARGE` | error | A quadrature stage — `method = laplace`, or `method = focei` with `n_agq > 1` — with `n_agq` above `MAX_AGQ_NODES` (21), where the Golub–Welsch rule loses accuracy. Re-checked here because a `FitOptions` built in code bypasses the parser's limit. A chain with no quadrature stage is refused too: it ignores `n_agq` but records it in the fit, where a `.fitrx` holding it does not load ([#1770](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1770)). |
| `E_AGQ_GRID_TOO_LARGE` | error | A quadrature stage — `method = laplace`, or `method = focei` with `n_agq > 1` — whose tensor grid of `n_agq^n_eta` nodes per subject exceeds `MAX_AGQ_GRID` (100,000). Lower `n_agq`, reduce the random effects, or use `saem` / `imp`. Under IOV the grid is `n_agq^(n_eta + K·n_kappa)`, with `K` the most occasions any subject has, so that check needs the data: `fit()` and `ferx check --data` raise it ([#1788](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1788)). |
| `E_AGQ_EVAL_ONLY` | error | `agq_eval_only = true` turns a `laplace` stage into a likelihood evaluator, so it needs a `laplace` stage in the chain and that stage must be the last one. Mid-chain, the reported `−2 log L` would be at parameters the next stage overwrites. |
| `E_FOCEI_NAGQ_UNSUPPORTED` | error | `method = focei` with `n_agq > 1` (the Gauss-Newton-anchored quadrature) on a model outside the analytic sensitivity scope, e.g. an ODE model without sensitivities or a pure TTE endpoint. Its anchor Hessian comes from the adjoint; `method = laplace` with `n_agq > 1` has no such restriction ([#251](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/251)). |
| `E_VI_NAGQ_UNSUPPORTED` | error | `n_agq > 1` set on a method chain that contains `vi` and no stage that uses a quadrature grid (`laplace` or `focei`). VI integrates over its variational posterior, so the option would do nothing. Remove `n_agq`, or chain `methods = vi, laplace`. |

#### Endpoints, IOV and VI

A method that cannot score the model's non-Gaussian endpoint or its inter-occasion variability.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_BINARY_GN_UNSUPPORTED` | error | `gn` or `gn_hybrid` anywhere in the method chain on a model with a `[binary_model]` (binary or categorical) endpoint. The Gauss-Newton gradient is built from the Gaussian residuals and ignores the logistic likelihood; use `focei`, `saem` or `imp`. |
| `E_BINARY_IOV_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `[binary_model]` (binary or categorical) endpoint on a model with inter-occasion variability (`n_kappa > 0`), whatever the method. The binary term enters the inner EBE objective but not the outer IOV objective, so estimates would be biased. |
| `E_CTMM_GN_UNSUPPORTED` | error | `gn` or `gn_hybrid` anywhere in the method chain on a model with a `[markov_model]` (CTMM) endpoint. The Gauss-Newton gradient ignores the Markov transition likelihood; use `focei`, `saem` or `imp`. |
| `E_CTMM_IOV_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `[markov_model]` (CTMM) endpoint on a model with inter-occasion variability (`n_kappa > 0`), whatever the method. The transition generator is built from the between-subject η only, so κ would be ignored. |
| `E_IMPMAP_IOV_UNSUPPORTED` | error | `method = impmap` (anywhere in a method chain) on a model with inter-occasion variability (`n_kappa > 0`). IMPMAP has no κ sufficient statistics or Ω~IOV~ M-step yet; use `saem` or `focei`. |
| `E_VI_MODEL_UNSUPPORTED` | error | `method = vi` (anywhere in a method chain) on a model whose likelihood VI's data term — the fixed-η Gaussian observation NLL — does not cover: one with a non-Gaussian endpoint (time-to-event, binary, categorical; under the `survival` feature), or an SDE (`[diffusion]`) model scored by the EKF. Use `laplace` / `saem` for the former, `foce` / `focei` for the latter. |
| `W_VI_OMEGA_UNANCHORED` | warning | A method chain containing `vi` sets both `vi_kl = mc` and `vi_omega_update = adam`. The closed-form Ω maximiser is disabled and the gradient replacing it is sampled, which is the configuration Janssen et al. (2024) report Ω fluctuating badly in. Keep `vi_omega_update = closed_form`, or raise `vi_mc_samples` substantially. |

#### Mixture, LTBS and IIV on residual error {#codes-mixture-ltbs-iiv-on-ruv}

Model features a method or an error model cannot represent. `fit()` refused each of these before [#1788](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1788) gave them a code; `ferx check` now reports them too.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_MIXTURE_METHOD` | error | A `[mixture]` model with a method its objective is not wired for: `method = focei` with `n_agq > 1`, an estimator other than `foce` / `focei` / `saem` / `bayes` / `imp` / `impmap`, or `bayes` with per-class `omega(k)` / `sigma(k)` overrides, since its Ω draw is shared across classes. Checked at every stage of the method chain. Block `fit_options`. |
| `E_IIV_ON_RUV_SHARED_ETA` | error | The `iiv_on_ruv` random effect is also used in `[individual_parameters]`. It must be a dedicated `omega`. Block `error_model`. |
| `E_IIV_ON_RUV_METHOD` | error | `iiv_on_ruv` with a non-interaction stage (`foce`, or `gn` without `interaction`) anywhere in the method chain. `Y = IPRED + EPS·EXP(ETA)` is an interaction model: use `focei`, `imp`, `impmap` or `saem`. Block `fit_options`. |
| `E_LTBS_UNSUPPORTED` | error | LTBS (`log_transform = true`) with a proportional or combined error, a per-CMT error model, or an SDE. The parser refuses all three, so only a `CompiledModel` built in code reaches it, through `fit()` or `check_model_options()`. Block `error_model`. |

#### Correlated residual error

A `block_sigma` correlated residual, or a residual `correlation` line, with a method or feature that cannot carry the correlation.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_BLOCK_SIGMA_METHOD_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `block_sigma` (correlated residual error) model whose method chain contains a stage outside `foce`, `focei`, `saem`, `imp`, `laplace` and `vi` — that is, `gn`, `gn_hybrid`, `impmap` or `bayes`. Reported once per chain. Not raised for a residual `correlation` line, which has its own scope check. |
| `E_BLOCK_SIGMA_CHAIN_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `block_sigma` model with at least one free (non-`FIX`) correlation, whose method chain places a stage that cannot read the estimated correlation (anything but `foce`, `focei`, `laplace`) after a stage that estimates it. That later stage would score the declared correlation instead; `FIX` the block, put the stage first, or drop it ([#847](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/847)). |
| `E_BLOCK_SIGMA_M3_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `block_sigma` (correlated residual error) model fitted with `bloq_method = m3`; the M3 censored-observation likelihood does not support a correlated residual covariance. |
| `E_BLOCK_SIGMA_FREM_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `block_sigma` (correlated residual error) model that is also a FREM model with covariate pseudo-observations; the combination is not supported. |
| `E_BLOCK_SIGMA_IIV_ON_RUV_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `block_sigma` (correlated residual error) model that also scales the residual error by a random effect (`iiv_on_ruv`); the combination is not supported. |
| `E_BLOCK_SIGMA_IOV_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `block_sigma` (correlated residual error) model with inter-occasion variability (`n_kappa > 0`), whatever the method. The IOV inner objective does not yet use the full residual covariance matrix. |
| `E_BLOCK_SIGMA_SDE_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `block_sigma` (correlated residual error) model with a `[diffusion]` block and a `saem` stage in the method chain. SAEM's data term omits the EKF process-noise variance, so its E-step and M-step would optimise different likelihoods; `foce` / `focei` support the combination. |
| `E_BLOCK_SIGMA_TTE_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `block_sigma` (correlated residual error) model that also declares a non-Gaussian endpoint (`[event_model]`, `[binary_model]` or `[markov_model]`), whatever the method. The joint likelihood accumulates the residual covariance diagonally and would silently drop the correlation. |
| `E_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_SCOPE` | error | A residual `correlation` line is fitted by `foce` and `focei` only. Refused with any other method anywhere in the chain, with `n_agq > 1`, with `bloq_method = m3`, with FREM covariate pseudo-observations, with a time-to-event / binary / categorical / Markov endpoint, with a mixture model, or with an SDE (`[diffusion]`) model. The message names the offending method or feature. |

#### Priors

A `prior(...)` the chosen method or covariance step would silently drop.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_PRIOR_METHOD_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `prior(...)` is in force but the last stage that estimates (a trailing evaluation-only `imp` or `laplace` does not count) is not one that applies parameter priors — only `foce`, `focei`, `laplace`, `gn` and `gn_hybrid` do. The fit would return the unpenalized estimates. Make one of those the last estimating stage (e.g. `methods = [saem, focei]`) or remove the prior. |
| `E_PRIOR_COV_METHOD_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `prior(...)` is in force and the covariance step runs with `covariance_method = s` or `rsr`. `S` is a sum of per-subject scores and a prior contributes one population-level score, so `s` reports the unpenalized standard errors and the `rsr` sandwich reports ones that are too small on every priored coordinate. Use `covariance_method = r` (the default) or `covariance = false`. |

### Data and dosing {#codes-data-and-dosing}

The dataset could not be read, or a dose / observation record is inconsistent with what the model expects.

#### Records and observations

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_DATA` | error | The `--data` file could not be read or parsed. |
| `E_MISSING_COVARIATE` | error | The model references a covariate not present in the data (case-sensitive). On block `covariates`, a column the `[covariates]` block declares is missing from the file. On block `simulation`, `run_model_simulate()`'s `[simulation]` design does not state a covariate the model reads ([#1788](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1788)). |
| `E_COVARIATE_NOT_NUMERIC` | error | A column the `[covariates]` block declares holds a value that is not a number. Block `covariates`. |
| `E_NONFINITE_DV` | error | A subject carries a non-finite (`NaN`/`Inf`) observation. Usually a population read by `read_population_for_simulation()` — a simulation input — passed to `fit()`. |
| `E_NO_SCORED_OBSERVATIONS` | error | The population has no record the likelihood scores: no Gaussian observation and no endpoint (TTE / binary / categorical / Markov) record on any subject. The data contribute nothing to the objective of such a fit, so no estimate can move off its initial value except under a `[priors]` or regularization penalty. `fit()` refuses it with the same message, where it used to return OFV 0 with the parameters at their initial values. Reported once for the population, after the more specific data codes, so `fit()` still names an unrouted endpoint (`E_ENDPOINT_NO_RECORDS`) or a non-finite `DV` first. When `[data_selection]` removed rows classed as observations, the message gives what it removed and names its clauses as the thing to check; otherwise it says what makes a row scored (`EVID = 0`, `MDV = 0` and a `DV`). Only `ferx check --data` reaches it; without a dataset there is nothing to count ([#1491](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1491)). |
| `W_MISSING_DV` | warning | One or more `EVID=0` rows had a missing `DV` (`.`/`NA`/blank) but were not marked `MDV=1`; they were skipped rather than scored as `DV=0`. |
| `W_COVARIATE_MISSING` | warning | A covariate column that exists has no value (every cell `.`, blank or `NA`) for some subjects, so it is `NaN` for them. Reported once per covariate, naming it and up to five of the subjects. A relation that reads it is then `NaN`, which makes the objective non-finite, or — through `log`, `sqrt`, `min`, `max` or a comparison — a finite value with no further warning. Impute the column, exclude the subjects, or guard the relation with `present(COV)`. See [Covariate Columns](../data-format.qmd#covariate-columns) ([#2041](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/2041)). |
| `W_DESIGN_DV` | warning | Simulation reader only: one or more `EVID=0` rows had a missing `DV` and were kept as design points to simulate at, so the dataset contributes more rows than a fit of the same file would. |
| `W_CENS_UNEXPECTED` | warning | An observation row's `CENS` cell is a whole number other than `-1` (above ULOQ), `0` (quantified) or `1` (below LLOQ), such as `7` or `-2`. Every engine reads only the flag's sign, so under `bloq_method = m3` a positive flag is scored on the lower tail, like `1`, and a negative one on the upper tail, like `-1`; under `bloq_method = drop` the row is scored as an ordinary observation. The message quotes the cell as written (`200`, not the `127` it saturates to) and is reported once per subject for each sign. It is not raised on a simulation design row with no `DV`, which is never scored. A cell that is **not a whole number** (`1.5`, `abc`, `inf`) is not this warning but a read error, reported as `E_DATA`, on a Gaussian observation row that carries a `DV` and that `[data_selection]` keeps; on a dose row, a row whose `DV` is missing, or a row the filter removes, the cell is not read ([#1496](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1496)). |
| `W_FILTER_COLUMN_ABSENT` | warning | A `[data_selection]` condition names a column the dataset does not have. The comparison never matches, so the condition does not select what was meant — and what that costs depends on the key it was written under: an `ignore` excludes nothing, an `accept` excludes **every** row. The message names the missing column(s) and lists the headers the file does have, so a typo (`ignore = Coment`) is visible rather than silent. `ferx check --data` reports it since [#1465](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1465); before that the check never compiled the clauses, so only a fit could raise it. |
| `W_DATA` | warning | A warning from the data reader whose message does not begin with its own `W_` code. `ferx check` relays each reader warning under the code its message opens with, and uses `W_DATA` only when there is none. |

#### Dose coverage

Whether the dataset delivers any drug at all. These read the dose records as a
set, so they say nothing about an individual row — for that see *Dose records*
below.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `W_AMT_NOT_DOSED` | warning | Record(s) carry `AMT != 0` but were **not** read as dose events, because `EVID` is neither 1 nor 4; their `AMT` was ignored. In a dataset with no `EVID` column a nonzero `AMT` is enough to infer a dose, so this is a file that has one. Reported with the record and subject counts. It wins over `W_NO_DOSES`, which is the generic backstop for a dataset carrying no `AMT` signal at all. See [#262](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/262). |
| `W_NO_DOSES` | warning | Zero dose events parsed across every subject, **although scored observations are present**. Silent when there are no scored observations (an all-`EVID=2`, covariate-only file is not a fit), and silent when any subject carries a non-Gaussian observation — a TTE / survival or discrete endpoint legitimately has no PK dose, so warning there would be a false positive. See [#262](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/262). |
| `W_ALL_DOSES_ZERO` | warning | An `AMT` column is present and at least one dose event was parsed, but every parsed amount is exactly zero. No drug enters the system, so the objective is flat and the parameters will not move from their initial values. A warning rather than an error because the column is there and a genuinely dose-free-but-`AMT`-columned dataset is conceivable. See [#753](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/753). |
| `E_DOSE_NO_AMT` | error | The dataset has dose records (`EVID` 1 or 4) but no `AMT` column, so every dose would have amount zero and the fit would run with no drug in the system. Usually the amount column has another name (e.g. `DOSE`); rename it to `AMT`. A read error, not a diagnostic of its own: `ferx check --data` reports it as `E_DATA` with this text ([#753](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/753)). |

#### Dose records

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `W_ADDL_MISSING_II` | warning | ADDL > 0 on a dose row but II is zero or missing; additional doses were not expanded. |
| `W_COMPARTMENT_FREE_DOSES` | warning | The dataset carries dose records but the `[structural_model]` is compartment-free (`$PRED`-equivalent), so no dose is applied and `AMT` / `RATE` / `SS` / `CMT` on those rows have no effect on the prediction. Reported once, with the dose-event count (after `ADDL` expansion) and the number of dosed subjects. Every dose-level check that would read the model's compartments is skipped for this class — a coded `RATE=-1` / `-2` row is not `E_MODELED_*_NO_PARAM` (a `D{n}` / `R{n}` the model cannot consume) and a `CMT=2` row is not `E_DOSE_CMT_OUT_OF_RANGE` (the placeholder one-compartment topology the parser installs) — so the rows land here instead ([#1443](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1443)). |
| `W_CMT_DEFAULTED` | warning | Dose and observation rows were assigned compartment 1 because the dataset did not say which one — no `CMT` column, or a cell that is missing (`.`/blank/`NA`) or not a compartment index. The message gives the row counts (plus the `ADDL`-expanded dose count when a defaulted row carried `ADDL`) and, for a present column, the offending spellings. Reported whenever `CMT` selects something on the model: more than one compartment a dose can reach — more than one `[odes]` state, **or** an analytical model whose `CMT=2` is a real target (an oral model's depot-bypassing central bolus, a 2-cpt model's peripheral) — **or** an observation-side dispatcher, a per-CMT `[scaling]` block, a `CMT=N:` error model, or a per-CMT `y[CMT=N]` readout on either engine, **or** a declared endpoint the row routes to (unless the model is endpoint-only and that endpoint is compartment 1, where the fallback is provably right), **or** a `[data_selection]` clause comparing `CMT`. Silent where `CMT` chooses nothing: `one_cpt_iv`, a one-state `[odes]` model, a compartment-free model, the transit / inverse-Gaussian absorption models, and a `[data_selection]` clause on any other column. Rows a `CMT`-reading filter clause *removed* are counted and named separately, since they never reach the dose / observation counts ([#1409](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1409)). Reporting a declared endpoint duplicates `E_ENDPOINT_NO_RECORDS` on an absent column, deliberately: an endpoint routes rows **by CMT**, and suppressing the warning hid a silent re-routing between endpoints on a bad *cell*, where that error cannot fire. NONMEM has no equivalent finding because `$MODEL` lets it declare `DEFDOSE`; ferx has no such declaration, so an absent column is a genuine ambiguity rather than a default ([#1009](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1009)). |
| `W_STEADY_STATE_II` | warning | SS=1 doses with missing / non-positive `II` (treated as non-SS). |
| `W_STEADY_STATE_INFUSION` | warning | SS=1 infusion whose length *after bioavailability* exceeds `II` (overlapping pulses; SS skipped) — the run-in's own test (#1281). |
| `W_STEADY_STATE_ABSOLUTE_TIME` | warning | An `SS=1` dose (`II > 0`) on a model whose `[odes]` right-hand side reads an **absolute** clock — `TAFD`, `T`/`t`, or the bare `TIME` built-in. The run-in standing in for the infinite past expands the dose train on a clock local to each cycle, so an absolute clock has no periodic steady state to converge to: `T`/`TIME` return a finite number that matches NONMEM's own steady-state routine but is 67 % from the same model's explicit dose train, and `TAFD` reads `NaN` whatever coefficient it carries. `TAD` is **not** included — it is bounded inside one dosing interval, so the run-in does reproduce its train and is anchored against NONMEM ([#1139](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1139)). Counted per dose that actually reaches the run-in, so an SS infusion the run-in itself skips — one whose length *after bioavailability* exceeds its own `II` — or a dose on a compartment outside the state vector is not swept up. Asked of the PK block only, so a `TIME`-reading joint PK-TTE hazard does not trigger it, and `TIME` read from `[individual_parameters]` is out of scope; one shape over-reports, see [Steady state with `TAFD` or `TIME`](../model-file/steady-state.qmd#steady-state-with-tafd-or-time). |
| `W_STEADY_STATE_INIT` | warning | The model declares an `[initial_conditions]` baseline and at least one subject has a steady-state (`SS=1`) dose. The steady-state closed form already assumes an infinite dose history, and the baseline is superposed on top as a separate decaying transient, which double-counts the starting amount. Remove the SS flag or the baseline unless that superposition is intended. |

#### Dose compartments

A dose whose `CMT` the model has no compartment for, or cannot infuse into.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_DOSE_CMT_OUT_OF_RANGE` | error | A dose record — bolus or infusion, zero amount included — whose `CMT` exceeds the number of compartments: the `[odes]` block's declared states, or the analytical model's compartments. Such a dose used to be silently dropped (ODE) or panic the event walk (analytical). Reported once per (bolus/infusion, compartment); not raised on a compartment-free model, nor on an analytical model whose population feeds no PK prediction. |
| `E_DOSE_CMT_NOT_INFUSABLE` | error | An infusion (`RATE > 0` or a modeled rate) with a nonzero `AMT` that names a compartment the model cannot infuse into — in practice `CMT=0`, NONMEM's default dose compartment, which is defined for a bolus but not for a zero-order input. Raised on `[odes]` models and the event-walk analytical models (not transit / inverse-Gaussian); reported once per compartment, with the subject and time of the first row. |

#### Dose attributes

Bioavailability `F`, lag time `ALAG`/`LAGTIME`, and the modeled infusion duration `D{n}` / rate `R{n}` behind a coded `RATE` — the values the engine applies *at* a dose event.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_DOSE_ATTR_DOUBLE_USE` | error | A dose attribute the engine applies at the dose event is *also* read by the model, so its value is applied twice. Bioavailability and lag are caught at parse time on **both** engines (message names `[odes]`, `[scaling]` or `[adaptive_dosing]`) — on ODE models via the name (`F`, `LAGTIME`/`ALAG`, `F{n}`/`ALAG{n}`/`LAGTIME{n}`), on analytical models via the `pk(..., f=…)` / `lagtime=…` mapping, where the remedy is to drop the mapping rather than rename. `D{n}`/`R{n}` are reported only when a coded `RATE=-2`/`-1` dose in the data lands on them. **Initial conditions are exempt on both engines** — `[odes] init(state) = …` and `[initial_conditions]` seed the state with the raw value and never consult a dose attribute, so a seed that reads one applies it exactly once ([#1046](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1046)). See [#993](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/993) and [#1004](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1004). |
| `E_NEGATIVE_LAGTIME` | error | A dose lag — `lagtime` / `ALAG{n}`, or a per-route `fn(..., lag=L)` on the compartment the dose lands in — is negative at the initial typical-value point (η = 0), at some dose record's own snapshot. NONMEM refuses the same run (`PK PARAMETER FOR ABSORPTION LAG IS NEGATIVE`, `PROGRAM TERMINATED BY OBJ`), and so do `fit()` and `ferx check`. The message names the subject, the compartment and the dose record. Use a positive-link parameterisation or a lower bound of 0 on the lag's `theta`. A lag driven negative mid-fit is not rejected; it starts that dose's input earlier, identically on every engine ([#1189](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1189)). |
| `W_NEGATIVE_LAGTIME` | warning | `predict()` / `simulate()` only: the same finding as `E_NEGATIVE_LAGTIME`, on entry points that run no data errors. The lag is applied as written, so the dose's input starts before its record time ([#1189](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1189)). |
| `E_DOSE_ATTR_NONFINITE` | error | A dose attribute the engine applies at the dose event — lag time (`lagtime` / `ALAG{n}`), bioavailability (`F` / `F{n}`), or a modeled infusion duration `D{n}` / rate `R{n}` behind a coded `RATE` — is `NaN` or infinite at typical values for some subject. Checked at **every dose record's own snapshot**: that record's covariate values and its `TIME`, which is where the engine reads the attribute ([#1235](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1235)). The message names the subject, the compartment, the attribute and the record. Usually a covariate relationship undefined for that subject: a covariate missing at that record (a missing value is `NaN`, which passes through arithmetic, `^` and `exp`), a fractional power of a negative value (`ALAG1 = TVLAG*(WT/70)^0.75` with a negative `WT`), or an exponential model on an unscaled covariate (`ALAG1 = TVLAG*exp(WT)`). `exp` and `^` are the two DSL operations with no domain guard (`/` by ~0 returns 0, and `log`/`sqrt` floor their argument; see [Values outside an operation's domain](../model-file/individual-parameters.qmd#values-outside-an-operations-domain)). Every attribute now has the same consequence: the subject's predictions come back `NaN`, which the estimator reads as a diverged solve. For a lag or `F` that has always been so — they make `dose.time + lag`, and every break derived from it, non-finite, so the timeline cannot be ordered. A non-finite `D{n}`/`R{n}` used to be the quiet exception, and it was the dangerous one: it never reached you as a `NaN` at all, because an infinite `D{n}` gives `rate = amt / D = 0` (not an infusion at all) and a `NaN` was clamped to the transient-`D ≤ 0` floor, so the dose was served as an instantaneous bolus and the fit returned finite but silently wrong numbers — measured 2.03x high against the correct infusion at one elimination half-time. Since [#1284](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1284) a non-finite `D{n}`/`R{n}` repels the subject like every other attribute, so this check is the fit-init front door rather than the only line of defence. See [#1189](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1189). |

#### Modeled infusion duration and rate

A coded `RATE=-2` (modeled duration `D{n}`) or `RATE=-1` (modeled rate `R{n}`) dose against the parameter that supplies it.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_MODELED_DURATION_NO_PARAM` | error | A dose codes `RATE=-2` (modeled infusion duration) into compartment `n`, but the model declares no `D{n}` in `[individual_parameters]`, so the duration has no value to read. Reported once per compartment, naming the first such dose. Add `D{n} = ...` or give the dose an explicit positive `RATE`. Not raised on a compartment-free model, which applies no dose. |
| `E_MODELED_RATE_NO_PARAM` | error | A dose codes `RATE=-1` (modeled infusion rate) into compartment `n`, but the model declares no `R{n}` in `[individual_parameters]`, so the rate has no value to read. Reported once per compartment, naming the first such dose. Add `R{n} = ...` or give the dose an explicit positive `RATE`. Not raised on a compartment-free model, which applies no dose. |
| `W_MODELED_DURATION_NONPOSITIVE` | warning | For a `RATE=-2` dose into compartment `n`, the modeled duration `D{n}` evaluated at that dose's typical-value snapshot (initial θ, η = 0) is at or below `1e-8`. It is clamped to that floor, so the dose arrives as a bolus-like spike rather than an infusion and the fit may converge to a wrong optimum. One warning per compartment; use a positive-link parameterisation such as `D1 = exp(...)`. |
| `W_MODELED_RATE_NONPOSITIVE` | warning | For a `RATE=-1` dose into compartment `n`, the modeled rate `R{n}` evaluated at that dose's typical-value snapshot (initial θ, η = 0) is at or below `1e-8`. It is clamped to that floor, so the dose is delivered as a near-zero trickle over a near-infinite duration and the fit may converge to a wrong optimum. One warning per compartment; use a positive-link parameterisation such as `R1 = exp(...)`. |

#### Absorption input-rate functions

A built-in absorption input-rate function in `[odes]` (`transit()`, `igd()`, `weibull()`, `zero_order()`, `first_order()`) against the doses that feed it. Checked at typical values at every dose record.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_ABSORPTION_DOMAIN` | error | A parameter of a built-in absorption input-rate function in `[odes]` is out of its domain at typical values (η = κ = 0), evaluated at every dose record's own snapshot so a covariate or `TIME`-reading expression is caught at any dose: transit `mtt ≤ 0` or `n < 0`, igd `mat` or `cv2 ≤ 0`, weibull `td` or `beta ≤ 0`, zero_order `dur ≤ 0`, first_order `ka ≤ 0`, or a non-finite per-route `lag=`. The message names the subject and dose record; only the first offender is reported. |
| `E_ABSORPTION_FRACTION` | error | A dose-splitting pathway fraction (`FR*fn(...)`) on a built-in absorption input-rate term is not in (0, 1], or the fractions on one compartment sum to something other than 1 (tolerance 1e-4), at typical values evaluated at each dose record. The message names the subject and dose record; only the first offender is reported ([#388](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/388)). |
| `E_ABSORPTION_RATE_ZERO_ORDER` | error | A non-SS infusion (`RATE > 0`) into a compartment fed by a `zero_order()` absorption function in `[odes]`. Infusing a zero-order window is a window-with-window convolution ferx does not yet implement; dose a bolus into it or use a density kernel. Not reported when `E_ABSORPTION_SS_INFUSION` already is. |
| `E_ABSORPTION_SS_INFUSION` | error | A steady-state infusion (`SS=1` with `RATE > 0`) into a compartment fed by a built-in absorption input-rate function in `[odes]`. Steady state and infusion-into-kernel are each supported alone but not together; rejected whatever the `II`, so an `II ≤ 0` row is not silently served as a single non-SS infusion. |
| `E_ABSORPTION_SS_LAG` | error | An `SS=1` dose with `II > 0` into a compartment fed by a built-in absorption input-rate function, where that compartment has a lag time — a compartment `lagtime` / `ALAG`, or a per-route `lag=` on a forcing feeding it. The steady-state seed cannot yet route the dose through the absorption kernel over the previous interval. Not reported when `E_ABSORPTION_SS_ZERO_ORDER` already is. |
| `E_ABSORPTION_SS_ZERO_ORDER` | error | An `SS=1` dose with `II > 0` into a compartment fed by a `zero_order()` absorption function in `[odes]`. A zero-order input is a spanning window, so its steady state needs a window-based equilibration ferx does not yet have; expand the run-in with explicit dose records or use a density kernel. |
| `E_ABSORPTION_DIFFUSION` | error | An `[odes]` model whose right-hand side uses a built-in absorption input-rate function (`transit()`, `igd()`, `weibull()`, `zero_order()`, `first_order()`) also declares a `[diffusion]` block. The SDE/EKF propagation does not apply the input-rate forcing, so the absorption term would be silently dropped; remove one of the two. |

#### Transit and inverse-Gaussian closed forms

The analytic `one_cpt_transit` / `two_cpt_transit` and `one_cpt_ig` / `two_cpt_ig` models, whose closed forms serve fewer dose shapes than an `[odes]` model and have no solution in the flip-flop regime. A model with an ODE twin is rerouted there; one without is refused.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_TRANSIT_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A transit absorption model (`one_cpt_transit` / `two_cpt_transit`) with a dose or model feature its closed form cannot serve. Always refused: a dose into a compartment other than the depot (`CMT` ≥ 2; `CMT=0` counts as 1), an `EVID=3/4` reset, and a steady-state infusion. Refused only when the model has no ODE twin to reroute to: IOV (`n_kappa > 0`), a `TIME`-dependent structural parameter, within-subject time-varying covariates, an infusion, or an `SS=1` dose — the last also when the depot carries a lag time, twin or not. |
| `E_TRANSIT_FLIP_FLOP` | error | A transit absorption model (`one_cpt_transit` / `two_cpt_transit`) with no ODE twin to reroute to whose typical-value (η = 0) parameters fall outside the closed form's convergence domain on some subject — the flip-flop regime (disposition rate ≥ `KTR = (n+1)/mtt`) or, for 2-cpt, coincident disposition eigenvalues — where it returns an identically-zero profile. Rewrite the model with an explicit `transit()` forcing in `[odes]`, or check the `MTT` / `CL` starts. `simulate_with_uncertainty()` also returns it when every parameter draw landed in that regime although the point estimate did not. |
| `W_TRANSIT_FLIP_FLOP` | warning | A transit absorption closed form (`one_cpt_transit` / `two_cpt_transit`) with an ODE twin has, at the initial typical values (η = 0) of at least one subject, a disposition rate (`CL/V`, or the 2-cpt fast rate α) at or above the transit rate `KTR = (n+1)/mtt`. ferx evaluates the equivalent `transit` ODE model for such parameters, which is correct but slower. Reported once, naming the first such subject. A twin-less model in the same regime is the error `E_TRANSIT_FLIP_FLOP` instead. |
| `E_IG_UNSUPPORTED` | error | An inverse-Gaussian absorption model (`one_cpt_ig` / `two_cpt_ig`) with a dose or model feature its closed form cannot serve. Always refused: a dose into a compartment other than the depot (`CMT` ≥ 2; `CMT=0` counts as 1), an `EVID=3/4` reset, and a steady-state infusion. Refused only when the model has no ODE twin to reroute to: IOV (`n_kappa > 0`), a `TIME`-dependent structural parameter, within-subject time-varying covariates, an infusion, or an `SS=1` dose — the last also when the depot carries a lag time, twin or not. |
| `E_IG_FLIP_FLOP` | error | An inverse-Gaussian absorption model (`one_cpt_ig` / `two_cpt_ig`) with no ODE twin to reroute to whose typical-value (η = 0) parameters fall outside the closed form's convergence domain on some subject — the flip-flop regime (disposition rate ≥ `1/(2·MAT·CV²)`) or, for 2-cpt, coincident disposition eigenvalues — where it returns an identically-zero profile. Rewrite the model with an explicit `igd()` forcing in `[odes]`, or check the `MAT` / `CV²` / `CL` starts. `simulate_with_uncertainty()` also returns it when every parameter draw landed in that regime although the point estimate did not. |
| `W_IG_FLIP_FLOP` | warning | An inverse-Gaussian absorption closed form (`one_cpt_ig` / `two_cpt_ig`) with an ODE twin has, at the initial typical values (η = 0) of at least one subject, a disposition rate (`CL/V`, or the 2-cpt fast rate α) at or above the IG abscissa `1/(2·MAT·CV²)`. ferx evaluates the equivalent `igd` ODE model for such parameters, which is correct but slower. Reported once, naming the first such subject. A twin-less model in the same regime is the error `E_IG_FLIP_FLOP` instead. |

#### Endpoint routing

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_ENDPOINT_UNROUTED` | error | A compartment the model declares as a non-Gaussian endpoint (`[event_model]`, `[binary_model]`, Markov) carries Gaussian observations: the population was read without endpoint routing (`read_nonmem_csv()` instead of `read_population_for()`), so the endpoint's rows would be scored as concentrations and its likelihood would contribute nothing. Raised by `fit()`, `simulate()`, `predict()`, `predict_categorical()`, `run_covariance()` and `run_sir()` ([#1199](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1199)). |
| `E_ENDPOINT_NO_RECORDS` | error | A declared non-Gaussian endpoint has no row routed to it anywhere in the data — typically the `CMT` column is missing, so every row reads as CMT 1. Raised by the entry points that run the likelihood — `fit()`, `ferx check`, `run_covariance()`, `run_sir()` — not by `simulate()` / `predict()`: a simulation template has no event rows by construction ([#1199](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1199)). |
| `E_ENDPOINT_TV_COVARIATE` | error | A covariate that varies within a subject — on any row, endpoint rows included ([#1854](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1854)) — is read by an endpoint that evaluates it once, at the subject's baseline: an analytic hazard's own parameters, any covariate under an ODE-accumulated (drug-driven) hazard, a `[binary_model]` linear predictor, a `[markov_model]` transition intensity, or — on a drug-driven (time-inhomogeneous) CTMM — an individual parameter the `[odes]` solve feeds into the states the intensities read ([#1854](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1854)). The block is the endpoint's (`event_model`, `binary_model` or `markov_model`), and the message names the covariate and the first subject. Raised by `fit()`, `ferx check`, `predict()`, `predict_survival()`, `predict_categorical()`, `simulate()`, and the post-fit re-scorers `run_covariance()` and `run_sir()` ([#1854](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1854)); `ferx check` reports it since [#1774](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1774), so a model `fit()` refused is no longer `valid: true` ([#741](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/741)). |
| `E_ENDPOINT_TIME_DEPENDENT_PK` | error | The `TIME` axis of the same freeze: an ODE-accumulated (drug-driven) hazard integrates the individual parameters at their TIME=0 values, so a `[individual_parameters]` value that reads `TIME` and reaches the hazard (through the `[odes]` right-hand side or an `init()` seed) would put the PK and hazard halves of the objective on different concentration curves ([#1853](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1853)). Also raised, fail-closed, for a hand-built `CompiledModel` missing the compiled programs the analysis reads. Block `event_model`. A function of the model alone, so `ferx check` reports it without `--data` (since [#1774](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1774)). Raised by `fit()`, `ferx check`, `predict()`, `predict_survival()` and `simulate()`; not by `predict_categorical()`, which never reads the frozen snapshot. The same code on block `markov_model` is the freeze on a drug-driven (time-inhomogeneous) CTMM generator, whose `[odes]` solve runs under the same TIME=0 snapshot ([#1918](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1918)); raised by `fit()`, `ferx check`, `run_covariance()` and `run_sir()`. |

#### Endpoint records {#codes-endpoint-records}

Records of a non-Gaussian endpoint that its likelihood cannot score, each of which used to fold into a silent sentinel objective. `fit()` refuses them, and `ferx check --data` reports them, since [#1788](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1788).

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_RTTE_RECORDS` | error | A repeated-event (`type = rtte`) endpoint's records: interval-censored, a non-finite `TIME`, an entry time after the record's `TIME`, or out of time order; under `clock = reset` also a right-censored row before a later record, or two events at one `TIME`. The message names the subject. Block `event_model`. The reader drops some of these rows on load, so mostly a `Population` built in code reaches it. |
| `E_BINARY_STATE` | error | A `[binary_model]` record whose DV is not 0 or 1. The reader accepts any non-negative integer on a discrete compartment, since it cannot tell binary from ordinal. Block `binary_model`. |
| `E_CTMM_RECORDS` | error | A `[markov_model]` (CTMM) record whose DV is not one of the declared `states`, or a subject whose CTMM observation times decrease (the reader sorts doses, not observations). Block `markov_model`. |

### Scaling, output and derived columns {#codes-scaling-output-and-derived}

An observed compartment is missing a scaling or error-model entry, a declared per-CMT entry matches no observation, or an `[output]` / `[derived]` name does not resolve.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_ODE_METHOD_LINEAR` | error | `ode_method = linear` was passed in a caller's fit options (`fit()`, `run_covariance`, `run_sir`) for a model that cannot take the exact linear path: it has no `[odes]` block, or an equation is nonlinear in the states, reads model time, or uses an absorption input function, or it is a `[diffusion]` model. The message names which. (The same option in the model file is a parse error with the same message.) |
| `E_PER_CMT_SCALING` | error | An observed compartment lacks a per-CMT scaling entry. |
| `E_PER_CMT_ERROR_MODEL` | error | An observed compartment lacks a per-CMT `[error_model]` entry. |
| `E_RUV_MAGNITUDE_NONPOSITIVE` | error | A custom residual-error magnitude in `[error_model]` — an expression multiplying a sigma, such as a `weight = ...` modifier — or a `power(SIGMA, P)` exponent evaluates to zero, a negative number or a non-finite value at some observation, at the model's initial θ. A zero magnitude collapses that row's variance onto the floor so it dominates the fit; a non-positive exponent changes the error model's form. The usual cause is a missing or non-numeric covariate cell. The first offending observation is reported. |
| `W_PER_CMT_UNMATCHED` | warning | The other direction of the two above: a compartment the model **declares** an entry for, that no observation is recorded on. One code for all three per-CMT channels — `[scaling] obs_scale[CMT=N]`, `[error_model] CMT=N:`, and a `y[CMT=N]` readout on either engine — with the channel and the dead compartments named in the message. A warning rather than an error because the entry is inert rather than wrong: nothing goes `NaN`, and a scaling block shared across studies may legitimately declare more compartments than one dataset exercises. The usual cause is on the data side, a missing or mis-mapped `CMT` column keying every observation to compartment 1; on a column-less dataset `W_CMT_DEFAULTED` **also** fires, for the defaulting itself, while this code names the entries the defaulting left dead. That reading is offered only when the observed set is consistent with it (every observation on compartment 1), so a model observed on compartment 2 is not sent to audit a column that is present and correct. `[data_selection]` is named as a candidate cause — rather than suppressing the finding, since a filter on any column can remove exactly the rows an entry needed — but only for the dead compartments the clause actually emptied, which `ExclusionSummary::obs_cmts_excluded` records; a clause that removed rows on some other compartment is not blamed. Silent on an observation-free population, so `ferx check` without `--data` does not report every declared entry as dead ([#1405](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1405)). |
| `E_READOUT_DEPOT_UNSUPPORTED` | error | An analytic `[scaling] y = …` readout reads the oral `depot` amount on a subject whose depot dose superposition cannot reconstruct: one with an EVID=3/4 reset ([#650](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/650)), or one dosing a compartment other than the default ([#375](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/375)). Block `scaling`. Raised by `fit()`, `ferx check` and `predict()`; `ferx check` reports it since [#1774](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1774). Reference only `central`, or use an ODE model. |
