| `E_DERIVED_NAME_CONFLICT` | error | A `[derived]` name clashes with a built-in sdtab column, theta, eta, or individual-parameter name. |
| `W_DERIVED_COVARIATE_SHADOW` | warning | A `[derived]` name shadows a covariate (allowed but may be confusing). |
| `W_DERIVED_STEP_IGNORED` | warning | `step=` given for a DV-based integral (ignored; DV integrals always use observation times). |
| `E_OUTPUT_UNKNOWN_COLUMN` | error | A name in `[output]` is not recognised as a covariate, individual parameter, or derived expression. |
| `W_OUTPUT_DUPLICATE` | warning | A name in `[output]` is already written to sdtab automatically (e.g. `TAFD`, `TAD`, an eta name). |

### Experimental and degraded paths {#codes-experimental-and-degraded}

The model runs, but on a path that is experimental or that quietly drops a capability.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `W_EXPERIMENTAL_SDE` | warning | The model uses stochastic differential equations (`[diffusion]`), an [experimental](../maturity.qmd) feature. The filter is covariance-only — the state mean is never corrected by the data — so see [What the filter does not do](../model-file/diffusion.qmd#what-the-filter-does-not-do). |
| `W_EXPERIMENTAL_NN` | warning | The model uses neural-network components (`[covariate_nn]`), an [experimental](../maturity.qmd) feature. |
| `W_SDE_RESET` | warning | EVID=3/4 resets under an SDE `[diffusion]` model are not honoured. |
| `W_ABSORPTION_TWIN_DECLINED` | warning | An analytic transit / inverse-Gaussian model's ODE twin could not be built, so the model stays closed-form with no ODE fallback. Subjects needing the fallback (time-varying covariates, a `TIME`-dependent parameter, IOV, SS or infusion doses, the flip-flop regime) are then rejected with an explicit error. The message carries the twin parser's own reason — most often an individual parameter named after a twin state (`CENTRAL`, `PERIPH`). See [#1008](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1008). |
| `W_SDE_LAGTIME` | warning | An absorption lag time on an SDE (`[diffusion]`) model is not honoured by the filter. |
| `W_NN_WEIGHT_DIRECT_REFERENCE` | warning | An expression references a generated `[covariate_nn]` weight or bias θ directly rather than through the network's declared outputs. The analytic NN θ-gradient assumes the weights reach the likelihood only through the network output, so it is disabled for the model and every θ uses finite differences (slower, still correct). `ferx check` currently shows this under `W_PARSE`. |

### Warnings a run records {#codes-run-warnings}

`ferx check` never reports these: they describe what happened while a run estimated or predicted, so they exist only as the code that opens a message in `FitResult.warnings` (or, where noted, in the `warnings` a `predict*` / `simulate*` call returns).

#### Estimation

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `W_STALLED_AT_INIT` | warning | The estimates never left the initial values. The test is the optimizer's own escape test when the result carries one (no packed coordinate moved by 1% of its scaled range), otherwise a comparison of the free θ, Ω and σ against their initial values at 1% relative. The reported objective is the objective of the initial values, even if `converged` is true. Suppressed for an evaluation-only run (`outer_maxiter = 0`). |
| `W_NO_FEASIBLE_EVAL` | warning | The outer optimizer finished without one feasible objective evaluation: every trial was rejected by the EBE convergence guard (`max_unconverged_frac`) or returned a non-finite objective. Nothing was minimised, the reported estimates are the ones the fit started from, and the fit is `converged: false`. The message names the cause and the remedy (`inner_maxiter` / `max_unconverged_frac`, or the record that poisons the objective). Not raised for a cancelled run. |
| `W_NONFINITE_OBJECTIVE` | warning | The objective at the final estimates is `NaN`, infinite, or at or above the `1e14` divergence cutoff, so the fit is demoted to `converged: false` whatever the optimizer's stop rule said; the message names which. Exempt: `method = vi` with `vi_final_ofv = none`, which publishes no objective by design. |
| `W_DEGENERATE_CL_V` | warning | The final estimates put a non-positive or non-finite `CL` or `V` on at least one dose, observation, EVID=2 or EVID=3/4 record of a 1-/2-/3-cpt IV / oral closed-form model, each record read under its own covariates and occasion. Both closed-form engines serve a non-positive or infinite value a concentration of 0, and a `NaN` one `NaN` once a dose has arrived; NONMEM would reject the record. The message names the subjects, the record count and the first offending `TIME`. See [Warnings](../warnings.qmd) and [#2104](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/2104). |
| `W_EBE_START_DEPENDENT` | warning | Three triggers. A cold re-solve of the EBEs at the final estimates scores worse than the reported objective by more than `1e-3·(1 + abs(OFV))`, or returns a non-finite objective ([#833](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/833)). A cold re-solve scores more than 0.05 OFV units below the objective the optimizer minimised, and no restart replaced the run; the fit is then reported `converged: false` ([#1565](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1565)). Or the `inner_screen` Sobol screen moved some subjects' EBEs to a lower individual objective than the descent from η = 0 reached; the message names them, the first ten and then a count ([#2013](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/2013)). |
| `W_VI_BAD_BASIN` | warning | At the end of a `method = vi` run, the excess of the sampled data term over its value at the variational means is more than 25 times the `Σ dᵢ/2` a posterior-shaped `q` would give. The ELBO is not a usable bound there, the optimizer has almost certainly settled in a bad basin, and the fit is reported `converged: false`. Re-run from better starting values, or chain `method = [focei, vi]`. |

#### Covariance step

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `W_COV_ANALYTIC_SALVAGE` | warning | The covariance step assembled the exact analytic R matrix for the subjects inside the analytic scope and finite-differenced the information terms of the subjects outside it, rather than moving the whole population onto the finite-difference stencil ([#1514](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1514)). The message names those subjects. |
| `W_COV_QUADRATURE_OBJECTIVE` | warning | A `saem` / `imp` / `impmap` estimate on a model with a non-Gaussian endpoint had its covariance R and S matrices taken on the 7-node adaptive Gauss–Hermite marginal (`method = laplace, n_agq = 7`) rather than on the FOCEI objective, whose minimum can sit far from that estimate ([#1781](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1781)). |
| `W_COV_QUADRATURE_DECLINED` | warning | The same kind of fit, where the quadrature marginal could not be used — a mixture, inter-occasion variability, or more than three random effects — so the standard errors are the FOCEI objective's curvature at a point that objective need not minimise ([#1781](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1781)). |
| `W_COV_ODE_TOLERANCE_NOT_TIGHTENED` | warning | An integrated model's covariance step, which finite-differences its R stencil or score matrix S, could not be run at `ode_reltol = 1e-6` / `ode_abstol = 1e-8` and ran at the fit's looser tolerance, so the standard errors may be inflated by integration noise (#520). A step that then fails reports this in its `Covariance step failed` message instead, without the code. |
| `W_COV_NN_PENALTY` | warning | A regularized `[covariate_nn]` fit (`nn_l2` / `nn_smooth`): under `covariance_method = r` / `rsr` the standard errors include the penalty's curvature (penalized-ML SEs, Info); under `s` they cannot represent it (Warning) ([#1352](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1352)). |
| `W_COV_RSR_ONE_SUBJECT_LEVELS` | warning | A successful `covariance_method = rsr` step on a model with a θ level block, profiled or not, where some estimated levels are read by a single subject (an MBMA block over `[STUDY, TIME]` with one subject per study). A `FIX` block and a `contrast = ref` reference level are constants with no SE, and are not counted. At the estimate such a level's own score is zero or nearly so, so its `rsr` SE is not usable: on `mbma_placebo` they are 1.5–4.8× below `r`'s. The message names the block, the count and an example level, and says to read those SEs from `r`. Raised by `fit()` and `run_covariance`, which replaces it with the step it reruns. |
| `W_COV_PROFILED_LEVELS_RESOLVED` | warning | `run_covariance` on a profiled fit whose level estimates are not the profile solve's at the other estimates, because they were edited after the fit. The step re-profiles the levels before it runs, and computes its matrix where that re-solve put them; the reported estimates and their SEs are then those re-solved levels, so a level moved onto its declared bound reports the bound as its estimate next to `at_bound: true`. The message counts the levels that moved, names the largest move, and says the objective and the EBEs are still the incoming fit's. Raised by `run_covariance` only, which replaces it with the step it reruns. |
| `W_COV_NON_STATIONARY_ESTIMATE` | warning | The covariance R matrix needed an eigenvalue floor (indefinite, or an eigenvalue under `max(1e-10·λ_max, 1e-12)`) at a `saem` / `imp` / `impmap` / `vi` estimate, which those methods never minimise the R objective at. A requested `r` / `rsr` covariance was replaced by `S⁻¹`, or the step failed when `S` was unavailable too ([#1781](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1781)). |

#### ODE solver

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `W_ODE_SOLVER_DIAGNOSTICS` | warning | The ODE solver statistics of that pass (post-fit predictions at the final estimates, or the predict/simulate call at the supplied parameters) show an unclean integration. That means steps clamped at the minimum step size that were kept, `ode_method = auto` stiff escalations that were rejected or whose fallback failed, unfinished segments kept, stiff-aborted or diverged segments, or a timeline abandoned as non-finite. The message carries the counters and names the pass. |
| `W_ODE_SOLVER_ESCALATION_NOTE` | warning | Informational (severity `Info` in `warnings_structured`). `ode_method = auto` escalated one or more integration segments to a stiff stepper, and nothing else went wrong: no escalation was rejected, no step clamped at the minimum step size, no segment was unfinished. Set `ode_method` explicitly to pin either stepper. |

#### Compartment reads in `[derived]`

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `W_DERIVED_CMT_IOV_UNSUPPORTED` | warning | A `[derived]` expression reads `compartments[i]`, and at least one subject of the fit carries IOV (kappa) parameters. The IOV prediction path computes no compartment states, so the expression is `NaN` for those subjects. |
| `W_DERIVED_CMT_TV_ANALYTICAL` | warning | The model has no `[odes]` block, a `[derived]` expression references `compartments[i]`, and at least one subject carries time-varying covariates, or an individual parameter reads `TIME` (#1855). Compartment states are not reconstructed for those subjects (baseline-parameter states would disagree with the time-varying `IPRED`), so the expression evaluates to NaN for them. |
| `W_DERIVED_CMT_TV_ODE` | warning | The model has an `[odes]` block, a `[derived]` expression references `compartments[i]`, and at least one subject carries time-varying covariates, or an individual parameter reads `TIME` (#1855). For those subjects the compartment states come from a pass that holds the disposition parameters at the first observation, so they are approximate; `IPRED` is exact. The message names which of the two causes the fit has. A reset alone, or an `[odes]` right-hand side that reads `TIME`, does not trigger it: those states are exact. |
| `W_DERIVED_CMT_RESET_ANALYTICAL` | warning | A `[derived]` expression reads `compartments[i]` on an analytical (non-`[odes]`) model where some subject has an `EVID=3/4` reset. Superposition is not valid across a reset, so those subjects' compartment states and compartment-based integrals are `NaN`; use an ODE model if states across resets are needed. |
| `W_DERIVED_CMT_ORAL_DEPOT_INFUSION_ANALYTICAL` | warning | A `[derived]` expression reads `compartments[i]` on an analytical (non-`[odes]`) model where some subject has a dose the closed-form superposition cannot place: an infusion into a compartment other than central (including a zero-order input into the oral depot) or a bolus into a compartment other than 1. Predictions stay exact, but those subjects' compartment states are `NaN`; use an ODE model for per-compartment amounts. |
| `W_DERIVED_INIT_ANALYTICAL` | warning | The model has no `[odes]` block, declares an `[initial_conditions]` baseline, and a `[derived]` expression references `compartments[i]`. The superposition state reconstruction does not seed the baseline, so compartment states are left empty and the expression evaluates to NaN; predictions are exact. Use an `[odes]` model with `init(...)` if compartment amounts are needed. |

### Codes only an entry point raises {#codes-entry-point}

`ferx check` never reports these: they refuse an option, a parameter set, a fit or a call that a model file and its data do not contain, or a model `fit()` accepts but the entry point cannot run. Each is the `code()` of the `EngineError` the entry point returns ([#1774](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1774)). They are not the only codes `ferx check` cannot reach: the θ length, parameter shape, fit-binding and population codes are too, and [matching on the code](../warnings.qmd#entry-point-error-codes) lists every code an entry point returns.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_CTMM_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A `[markov_model]` endpoint reached `predict()` with no continuous observation to predict, or `simulate()` or `run_model_simulate()`: neither has a state-occupancy path yet ([#820](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/820)). `fit()` supports the model. Block `markov_model`. |
| `E_TTE_NOT_SIMULATABLE` | error | A TTE endpoint the event-time simulator cannot draw for this population: more than one repeated-event stream on a subject, a repeated-event cause beside a single-event one, an EVID=3/4 reset under a repeated-event or a drug-driven hazard, or left truncation under a drug-driven hazard. Also a repeated-event or drug-driven TTE endpoint on `simulate_with_uncertainty()`, which needs a horizon and takes none; the message names `simulate_with_options()`, which takes one. Block `event_model`. |
| `E_SIMULATE_HORIZON` | error | The simulation horizon is missing where a repeated-event or drug-driven TTE endpoint needs one (on an entry point that takes a horizon), is not finite and positive, or lies below a subject's entry time. `run_model_simulate()` returns it for a `[simulation]` block with a TTE endpoint of any kind and no `horizon`, the time its template rows are censored at ([#1788](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1788)). |
| `E_PROPENSITY_INPUT` | error | Propensity-score matching was requested on a population it cannot compute posthoc etas from: empty, a subject with no observations, a subject with a non-finite `DV`, or a `[mixture]` model. |
| `E_NESTED_LEVEL_SIMULATE_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A model with nested levels (more than one `level`) reached an adaptive-dosing entry point. Its kappa stream draws one kappa per occasion, and a kappa at an outer level has to be drawn once per group. `fit()`, `simulate()` and `simulate_with_uncertainty()` support the model. Block `parameters`. |
| `E_THETA_LENGTH` | error | An entry point taking a parameter vector was handed a θ whose length is not the model's, and refused it rather than read it by position. Raised by `fit()` on its initial parameters, the `predict*`, `simulate*` and adaptive entry points, `compute_npde_npd`, and `run_sir` / `run_covariance` on a fit whose θ does not fit the model they run on ([#1614](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1614), [#1615](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1615), [#1774](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1774)). On a level-block model the message says the θ count is set by the bound data. |
| `E_PARAM_SHAPE` | error | An entry point was handed an Ω, σ or Ω~IOV~ whose dimension is not the model's, an Ω~IOV~ on a model with no κ, or none on a model with κ, and refused it rather than read it by position ([#1764](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1764), [#1774](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1774)). Raised by `fit()`, the `simulate*` and adaptive entry points, `simulate_with_uncertainty`, `compute_npde_npd`, `fitted_params_from_result` (Ω~IOV~), and `run_sir` / `run_covariance` (σ and Ω~IOV~). `fit()` also returns it for `init_params` with no per-class Ω/Σ on a `[mixture]` model ([#1788](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1788)). Not by `predict*`, which read none of the three. |
| `E_THETA_LEVELS_UNBOUND` | error | A `theta NAME[...]` level block was never bound to data, so it has no levels and every value gathered from it is `NaN` — a `CompiledModel` assembled in code that skipped the binder. Call `bind_theta_levels` after reading the population (`bind_from_fit` with the fit's `data_bindings` when predicting with a fit's θ), use a file entry point that binds for you, or declare the block as `theta NAME[N](...)` indexed by your own column. |
| `E_FREM_NON_GAUSSIAN_ENDPOINT` | error | `prepare_frem()` or `transform_dataset_for_frem()` was handed a model that declares a non-Gaussian endpoint (`[event_model]`, `[binary_model]` or `[markov_model]`). The FREM dataset is written from Gaussian rows only, so the endpoint's records would be dropped; the message names the endpoint CMTs. Run FREM on the PK model without that block. |

A missing Ω~IOV~ on `simulate()` reuses an existing code, since the cause is the same: it is `E_PARAM_SHAPE`, the parameter-shape code the other entry points return (see [matching on the code](../warnings.qmd#entry-point-error-codes)).

#### File entry points {#codes-file-entry-points}

Refusals of the file entry points (`fit_from_files()`, `prepare_run()`, `run_model_with_data()`, `run_model_simulate()` and their variants, which `ferx` runs) and of `fit()` itself, for inputs `ferx check` does not read ([#1788](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1788)).

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_DATA_PATH_MISSING` | error | No data path was given and the model file has no `[data]` block. `ferx check` without `--data` skips its data checks instead of refusing. `resolve_data_path()` returns the same text as a `String`. |
| `E_SIMULATION_DESIGN` | error | A `[simulation]` design that gives the model nothing to observe: no `times` for a continuous (residual-error) or `[binary_model]` endpoint, or no `times` and no TTE endpoint to observe at a `horizon`. Block `simulation`. A design that does not state a covariate the model reads is `E_MISSING_COVARIATE` on block `simulation`, and one with a TTE endpoint and no `horizon` is `E_SIMULATE_HORIZON`. |
| `E_IOV_SINGLE_OCCASION` | error | A derived `iov_occasion` rule (`dose` or `time(...)`) gives every subject at most one occasion, so the per-occasion κ cannot be told from the η. Raised by `fit()` once it has derived the occasions, by `ferx check --data` (which derives the model's rule on the data with the same message), and by `run_model_simulate()` on its `[simulation]` template before simulating ([#2052](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/2052)), where the message names only `iov_occasion = time(...)`. Block `fit_options`. |

#### Simulation warnings

Warnings a `simulate*` call (or `compute_npde_npd_diag`, which simulates its reference distribution) returns in its `warnings`, prefixed with the code. The simulation still completes.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `W_IOV_NO_OCCASIONS` | warning | The model declares kappa (IOV) parameters and an Ω_IOV is supplied, but some subjects carry no occasion label once `iov_occasion` has been applied. Those subjects get no κ draw and are simulated (or, from `compute_npde_npd_diag`, have their NPDE/NPD reference distribution simulated) at κ = 0. Silent when no Ω_IOV is supplied. |
| `W_FREM_DRAWN_ETA` | warning | A FREM model was simulated with each subject's η drawn from Ω, covariate η included: by `simulate_with_options_diag()` without `match_method`, by `simulate_with_uncertainty_diag()`, or by an adaptive simulation for the subjects with no supplied η. A FREM model links its covariates to the PK only through Ω, so those subjects' PK follows the drawn covariate η, not their own covariate values, and their `FREMTYPE` rows report the drawn covariate value. Silent on a non-FREM model (#2245). |
| `W_SIMULATED_FLIP_FLOP` | warning | On a transit or inverse-Gaussian absorption closed form with no ODE twin, some simulated individuals with a positive dose before their last observation were evaluated at a sampled η inside the flip-flop regime (or the 2-cpt confluent-eigenvalue corner). There the closed form clamps the dose-driven concentration to zero, so their rows carry no contribution from their doses and still enter every summary. The message gives the count out of the eligible individuals; rewrite the model as an explicit ODE to simulate them. The NPDE/NPD reference distribution reports the same count for its own replicates (#1928). |
| `W_UNCERTAINTY_DRAWS_SKIPPED` | warning | Some parameter draws of `simulate_with_uncertainty` put a transit or inverse-Gaussian closed form with no ODE twin into the flip-flop regime at typical values, where it has no solution, so those draws were not simulated. The message lists them. The remaining draws exclude that tail of the parameter uncertainty, so prediction intervals built from them are biased. If every draw is skipped the call is refused instead. |
| `W_RTTE_DEGENERATE` | warning | While simulating a repeated-event (RTTE) stream, a subject's expected number of events before the horizon is non-finite or exceeds 1,000,000, so the stream is skipped; or a stream that passed that check produced more than 1,000,000 events, so it is truncated. Either way the subject is censored at the horizon and the rest of the population still simulates. Check the hazard parameters and covariate values. |
| `W_TTE_DEGENERATE_HAZARD` | warning | While simulating a time-to-event endpoint with an analytic hazard, a subject drew a non-positive or non-finite effective hazard rate. No event is generated and the subject is censored at the observation window. Under competing risks it is raised for each analytic cause whose draw degenerated when the subject ends censored. Check the hazard parameters and covariate values. |

#### Adaptive dosing {#codes-adaptive}

`simulate_adaptive()` and `simulate_adaptive_from_spec()` refuse most of these before any subject is simulated. The rest come from the driver once it runs, when they depend on the resolved doses, the break timeline or what the controller returned ([#1983](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1983)).

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_ADAPTIVE_UNSUPPORTED` | error | A model the adaptive-dosing driver cannot simulate faithfully (no `[odes]` block, an SDE, a covariate-selected `[error_model]`, a residual `correlation` line, a log-transformed (LTBS) error model — [#2129](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/2129)), an `auc_target` on a subject with a time-varying covariate, IOV or a reset, or a pre-scheduled base regimen with an EVID=3/4 reset under a time-varying covariate or IOV, refused before any subject is simulated. Once the driver runs ([#1983](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1983)): a base dose under a time-varying covariate or IOV that is not a plain bolus or infusion into a plain compartment, a dose lag or infusion duration that is not finite, or an `[odes]` right-hand side that reads `TAD` / `TAFD` before any dose. The block is the one at fault, when there is one. |
| `E_ADAPTIVE_OPTIONS` | error | `AdaptiveSimulateOptions` with no usable schedule (`decision_times` empty, not finite, not strictly increasing, or longer than `max_decisions`), a monitor on a compartment the model does not have, a `Dv` monitor on a compartment no `[error_model]` covers, or `decision_times` / `monitors` set alongside an `[adaptive_dosing]` spec that owns them. These are refused before any subject is simulated. Once the driver runs ([#1983](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1983)): two of a subject's times (decision, observation, EVID=2, reset or base-dose) within 1e-15 of each other without being equal, which the driver cannot tell apart. |
| `E_ADAPTIVE_CONTROLLER_ACTION` | error | The controller returned an action the driver refuses ([#1983](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1983)): a dose into compartment 0 or one past the model's states, an amount that is negative or not finite, an infusion rate that is not positive and finite, a dose into a compartment fed by a built-in input-rate function or carrying a lag, or a `Stop` followed by another action. The controller is the caller's code, so this is a refusal of the input, although only a simulation can reach it. On `simulate_adaptive_from_spec()` the controller is compiled from the spec's `route`, so the same refusal is `E_ADAPTIVE_SPEC` there. A non-finite amount computed from a diverged ODE state is not this code: the driver refuses a non-finite state, or a monitor that reads a non-finite value, before the controller runs, as an uncoded runtime error naming the states or the monitor ([#1578](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1578)). |
| `E_ADAPTIVE_SPEC` | error | An `[adaptive_dosing]` spec that does not compile against the model: an invariant the block parser checks (on a spec built in code), an `assay_cmt` out of range or with no `[error_model]` to draw the assay from, a `route` compartment out of range or fed by a built-in input-rate function, or an `observe` expression that does not compile. Once the driver runs, a `route` dose it refuses, such as one into a compartment with a dose lag. Block `adaptive_dosing`. |
| `E_SUPPLIED_ETAS` | error | Per-subject η supplied to an adaptive run that cannot be used as given ([#1594](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1594)). From `SuppliedEtas::from_table` or `from_fit`: IDs and rows that differ in count, a row that is not one finite value per named η, a repeated subject ID, or a fit whose η names are not the model's. From `simulate_adaptive_with_inputs` / `simulate_adaptive_from_spec_with_inputs`, before any subject runs: a `[mixture]` model (the run draws each subject's mixture class, so a fit's η̂ could be simulated under another class), η names that are not the model's in the model's order, or a simulated subject with no supplied η under `UnmatchedSubjects::Refuse` (the default), listing up to ten IDs. See [Supplied individual values](../model-file/adaptive-dosing.qmd#supplied-individual-values). |

An `[adaptive_dosing] observe` covariate the data lack reuses `E_MISSING_COVARIATE` (block `adaptive_dosing`), the code `ferx check` gives a model covariate missing from the data.

#### Post-hoc steps on a fit {#codes-post-hoc}

`run_sir()` and `run_covariance()` take a fit, and refuse one whose inputs they cannot recover or verify ([#1774](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1774)). `ferx check` has no fit, so it raises none of these. `simulate_with_uncertainty()` also rebuilds a fit's parameters, and refuses a `[mixture]` fit's override values with the same two codes. It draws from the fit's covariance matrix (asymptotic method) or its kept SIR resamples, and refuses one the fit does not carry, or an empty pool, as `E_FIT_INPUT_MISSING`, and one that is not the size of the model's packed parameters as `E_FIT_INPUT_MODEL` ([#2044](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/2044)).

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_FIT_INPUT_MISSING` | error | An input the step needs was neither passed nor recorded on the fit: the model file's path (no model passed), the data file's path (no population passed), SIR's covariance matrix, the population of an IOV model passed as a model on a fit that records no reader settings, the occasion rule of an IOV fit saved before ferx recorded one, on a population that carries no occasion labels, or the fitted values of a `[mixture]` fit's per-class overrides, on a fit that records neither them (`mixture_overrides`) nor a packed estimate holding them. |
| `E_FIT_INPUT_CHANGED` | error | The model or data file the step re-reads no longer has the SHA-256 the fit recorded. |
| `E_FIT_INPUT_MODEL` | error | The model the step would run on is not the one the fit was made with: a model passed in bound with other data-derived bindings than the fit's, a model passed in whose covariate statistics the population does not reproduce (on a fit that records no bindings), a model whose η count is not the width of the fit's per-subject η̂, a `[mixture]` fit whose recorded override values are malformed, or which records none and whose packed estimate has another layout or no longer reproduces its reported estimates, or a covariance matrix that is not the size of the model's packed parameters. |
| `E_SIR_OPTIONS` | error | SIR settings `run_sir()` cannot run with: `sir_resamples` above `sir_samples`, a `sir_df` that is not a valid Student-t degrees of freedom, or `sir_scale = natural` on a model with `prior(...)`. A `sir_df` below 1 is refused as `[fit_options]` refuses it, and is refused by `fit()` and `ferx check` up front whenever `sir = true` or `covariance_fallback = sir` ([#1770](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1770)); otherwise `fit()` with `sir = true` reports the same text as a `SIR failed:` warning instead. |
| `E_SIR_NOTHING_TO_SAMPLE` | error | every estimated parameter of the fit is FIX (θ, Ω and σ, and Ω_IOV, `block_sigma` correlations and `[mixture]` overrides where the model has them), so `run_sir()` has nothing to sample. Block `parameters`. `fit()` with `sir = true` reports the same text as a `SIR failed:` warning instead. |
| `E_ODE_SOLVER_OPTIONS` | error | ODE solver settings on a `FitOptions` built in code that no solver can run with: an `ode_reltol` or `ode_abstol` that is not finite and positive, `ode_max_steps = 0` ([#2044](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/2044)), or `ode_stiff_abort_after = Some(0)`, which `[fit_options]` spells as off ([#1770](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1770)). Refused on an analytic model too, since every fit records these settings. Raised by `fit()`, `run_sir()` and `run_covariance()`; `run_sir_core()` returns the same text as a `String`. A model file's `[fit_options]` never gets this far: the parser refuses the same values as `E_PARSE`. |
| `E_LOGIT_THETA_OUT_OF_RANGE` | error | A free θ used as `inv_logit(logit(θ) + ETA)` whose estimate is not strictly inside (0, 1), so it has no logit-scale draw ([#2044](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/2044)). Only a declared upper bound above 1 lets the estimate get there; the suggestion is to declare one below 1 and refit. Block `parameters`. Raised by `simulate_with_uncertainty()` with the asymptotic method and by `run_sir()`. Its `to_string()` ends with the suggestion; `run_sir_core()` returns that text as a `String`, and `fit()` with `sir = true` reports it as a `SIR failed:` warning. |

The θ count and the Ω, σ and Ω~IOV~ shape of a fit against the model are `E_THETA_LENGTH` and `E_PARAM_SHAPE`, the codes every entry point gives a parameter vector of the wrong shape. A population that is not the fit's is `E_POPULATION_MISMATCH`, or `E_FIT_SUBJECTS_MISMATCH` when the fit's per-subject rows are what is wrong.

When the step re-reads the model or data file, a failure is the one `ferx check` reports on the same file, with the same code and block: `E_MODEL_READ`, the parse codes, `E_DATA`, `E_MISSING_COVARIATE`, `E_COVARIATE_NOT_NUMERIC`, and `E_PARSE` on `data_selection` for a recorded selection clause that no longer compiles. The message is the read's own: an `E_DATA` refusal has no `Failed to read data file` lead.

##### The population a step runs on

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `E_POPULATION_MISMATCH` | error | A population handed to, or re-read by, a post-hoc step is not the one the fit was given ([#1685](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1685)): another subject list, other covariate columns, or a subject whose records, doses or covariate values differ. Raised by `run_sir`, `run_covariance` and `PopulationFingerprint::verify`; the message names what differs. Pre-empted by `E_ENDPOINT_UNROUTED` and `E_THETA_LEVELS_DATA_UNBOUND`, whose fix is a reader or a binder. |
| `E_FIT_SUBJECTS_MISMATCH` | error | The population matches the fit's fingerprint, but the fit's per-subject results (`fit.subjects`), which `run_sir` / `run_covariance` read by position, are another count or another order ([#1868](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1868)). Reachable when a front end rebuilds a fit from separate fields; a `fit()` result carries both from one population. Without a current fingerprint the same mismatch is `E_POPULATION_MISMATCH`. |

## Line-number caveat

`line` is currently **block-level**: when present it points at the `[block]`
header that owns the finding, not the exact offending token or column. A finding
that is not attributable to a single block (for example a missing-covariate
error, where the reference may appear in several blocks) omits `line`. A missing
*required* block omits `line` too, since the block has no header in the source.
Token/column-level spans are a possible future enhancement.
